subject: dsa
title: Gas Station
summary: Look at net = gas - cost. A loop is possible only if the total net is non-negative, and then the unique start is just after the last point where the running tank dipped below zero.
problem: At each station you gain gas[i] and spend cost[i] to reach the next. Find the starting station from which you can complete the loop, or -1.

steps.caption: At station i you gain gas[i] and pay cost[i] to move on. Work with net = gas - cost: [-2, -2, -2, 3, 3]. A full loop needs the total net to be >= 0.
The total net here is 0, so a solution exists and is unique. Now find it by tracking the tank, resetting the start whenever it goes negative.
Begin at index 0. Across stations 0, 1, 2 the running tank keeps falling below zero, so none of them can be the start.
Each time the tank dips below 0, the start must be the very next station. That moves the candidate start to index 3.
From index 3 onward the tank only rises: 3, then 6. It never goes negative.
Since the total net is non-negative, station 3 completes the loop. The answer is to start at index 3.
